title: Thomas Sankara Speaks
author: Thomas Sankara
desc: Discursos del 'Che Guevara africano': cuatro años de revolución en Burkina Faso.
tesis: Thomas Sankara, presidente de Burkina Faso de 1983 a 1987, realizó en cuatro años lo que la mayoría de los líderes africanos no logró en décadas: vacunó a 2.5 millones de niños, plantó 10 millones de árboles contra la desertificación, prohibió la mutilación genital femenina, construyó escuelas y hospitales, y se negó a pagar la deuda externa. Su discurso ante la OUA en 1987 — 'la deuda no se puede pagar' — es uno de los momentos más poderosos de la historia del Tercer Mundo. Fue asesinado tres meses después por su propio compañero Compaoré, con complicidad francesa. Sus discursos son un programa de gobierno antiimperialista, feminista y ecologista avant la lettre.
ideas: Sankara demostró que un país pobre puede transformarse radicalmente en cuatro años si hay voluntad política y honestidad.
'La deuda no se puede pagar y no se debe pagar' — Sankara desafió al FMI y al neocolonialismo financiero en la cara.
Fue feminista en acción: prohibió la mutilación genital, promovió a mujeres a cargos de poder, denunció el patriarcado como herramienta colonial.
Fue asesinado por su propio compañero con complicidad francesa — el patrón de siempre: las revoluciones tercermundistas mueren por traición interna y conspiración imperial.
contexto: Sankara (1949-1987) fue asesinado a los 37 años. Francia, que perdía control sobre su excolonia, facilitó el golpe de Compaoré que gobernó 27 años después. En 2022, un tribunal condenó a Compaoré in absentia por el asesinato. Sankara es hoy ícono panafricano comparable al Che.

conexiones.razon: Fidel y Sankara son paralelos: revoluciones tercermundistas que desafían al imperio con programas de soberanía.
Rodney explicó el subdesarrollo de África; Sankara intentó revertirlo en la práctica.
Lo que Galeano documentó para América Latina — saqueo imperial — Sankara lo enfrentó directamente en África.

quotes.text: Imperialism is everywhere. Through the culture that it spreads, through its misinformation, it gets us to think like it does, it gets us to submit to it, and to go along with all its manoeuvres. For goodness' sake, we must stand in imperialism's way.

tl: Sankara toma el poder en Alto Volta

On 4 August 1983, some 250 soldiers led by Captain Blaise Compaoré marched from an insurgent military base in Pô to the capital of Ouagadougou. The regime of Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo was overthrown in a popular uprising.
Proclamación del Consejo Nacional de la Revolución

Today, 4 August 1983, the patriotic and progressive soldiers, non-commissioned officers, and officers have thus restored the honour of our people and their army and have given them back their dignity.
Discurso de Orientación Política

Our people went through the test of heroic struggles and finally triumphed on the now historic night of 4 August 1983. The revolution has been irreversibly marching forward in our country now for almost two months.
Reforma agraria del CNR

The agrarian reform will aim to: Increase labour productivity through better organisation of the peasants and the introduction of modern agricultural techniques in the countryside. Develop a diversified agriculture.
Alto Volta pasa a llamarse Burkina Faso

On 4 August 1983, a popular uprising in the West African nation then known as Upper Volta initiated one of the most profound revolutions in Africa's history. A year later the people of Upper Volta adopted the name Burkina Faso – the Land of Upright Men.
Sankara en Harlem antes de la ONU

That's why I've always said – and I'll say it again – our White House is in Black Harlem. There are many who think Harlem is a dump. But there are also many of us who believe that Harlem will give the African soul its true dimension.
Sankara ante la Asamblea General de la ONU

I speak not only on behalf of my beloved Burkina Faso, but also on behalf of all those who are in pain somewhere. I speak on behalf of the millions of human beings who are in ghettos because they have black skin.
Día de la Mujer: emancipación femenina

In the battle to build a new society, which is a revolutionary battle, the conduct of these men places them on the side of reaction and counter-revolution. For the revolution cannot triumph without the genuine emancipation of women.
Frente unido contra la deuda en Addis Abeba

We believe analysis of the debt should begin with its roots. The roots of the debt go back to the beginning of colonialism. Those who lent us the money were those who colonised us. This debt has nothing to do with us. That's why we cannot pay it.
Si pagamos, moriremos: Sankara en la OUA

The debt cannot be repaid, first of all, because, if we don't pay, the lenders won't die. Of that you can be sure. On the other hand, if we do pay, we are the ones who will die. Of that you can be equally sure.
Homenaje al Che en Uagadugú
Che Guevara was cut down by bullets, imperialist bullets, under Bolivian skies. And we say that for us, Che Guevara is not dead. It's true, you cannot kill ideas. Ideas do not die.
Asesinato de Sankara

On October 15, 1987, Capt. Blaise Compaoré led a military coup serving the interests of those whose property and class domination were threatened. Sankara and twelve of his aides and bodyguards were assassinated and the revolutionary government destroyed.
